newsitem.title: FRANCE: French daily papers squeeze seen worse in 1997.
newsitem.headline: French daily papers squeeze seen worse in 1997.

text.p: The economic squeeze being suffered by daily newspapers in France will worsen in 1997 compared to 1996, Institut Xerfi said in a study on the management and performance of the daily press in 1997.
It said that even with austerity management and restructuring, there would be no recovery until 1998.

"Efforts to adapt will not prevent a further erosion of margins and results in 1997 -- current profit before tax will fall by nearly 13 percent -- but these efforts will nevertheless radically limit the size (of the erosion)," Xerfi said in the report.

"We can expect a significant recovery in accounts from 1998. External shocks will have been absorbed, but the price of this will have been profound changes in the management of these companies," it said.

This year the price of raw materials will tend to be higher, and interest rates will continue to fall -- although this penalises companies which have strong cash balances due to subscription income, Xerfi said.
But readership will continue to decline and companies' margin to manoeuvre will be very limited, it said.
